item.title: Goosebumps The Musical: Phantom of the Auditorium — Fri Oct 30, 6:30 PM — Waldron Arts Center
item.description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Goosebumps The Musical: Phantom of the Auditorium ” on stage October 30th- November 15th at the Waldron Auditorium.
Get ready for a frightfully fun adventure with Goosebumps The Musical, based on the wildly popular books by R. L. Stine! When Brooke and Zeke are cast in their school’s spooky new play, The Phantom, they start to wonder if the show is actually cursed. As strange messages appear and rehearsals are disrupted by a mysterious masked figure, they must uncover the truth: is it all an elaborate prank… or is their theater truly haunted? Full of catchy songs, laugh-out-loud moments, and just the right amount of Halloween-season chills, this musical mystery is perfect for kids, tweens, and grown-ups who remember reading by flashlight. Fun for all ages!
See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/goosebumps/ https://seeconstellation.org/k

item.title: The Harder They Come | New Americas Cinema — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Reggae superstar Jimmy Cliff is Ivan, a rural Jamaican musician who journeys to the city of Kingston in search of fame and fortune. Pushed to desperate circumstances by shady record producers and corrupt cops, he finally achieves notoriety—as a murderous outlaw. Boasting some of the greatest music ever produced in Jamaica, The Harder They Come brought the catchy and subversive rhythms of reggae and the Rastas to the world. [120 min; crime, drama, musical; English]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Postmodern Panic: Meta-Horror Double Feature with Scream + Cabin in the Woods | Friday Night Frights — Fri Oct 30, 10:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Scream (Wes Craven, USA, 1996): The horror blockbuster that jumpstarted a franchise that is still going strong, Scream follows a series of mysterious deaths in a small town as an offbeat group of friends become the target of a masked killer. As the body count rises, the kids must learn "the rules" of horror films to survive. [111 min; horror; English]
Cabin in the Woods (Drew Goddard, USA, 2011): When five college friends arrive at a remote forest vacation cabin, little do they expect the horrors that await them. One by one, they fall victim to backwoods zombies, soon discovering that there is more going on than meets the eye. [95 min; horror; English]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Oct 31 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Oct 31 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Oct 31 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: As part of the America 250 (https://bloomington.iu.edu/campus-life/events/america-250/) initiative, the Lilly Library is proud to present an expansion of our Declaration of Independence exhibition, focusing on the 56 signatories. IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, Th

item.title: Award Challenge: Game Day at the Art Museum — Sat Oct 31, 11:00 AM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Bloomington knows a thing or two about trophies now. For the home game this Saturday, the Eskenazi Museum of Art is handing the hardware to you. Pick up a trophy at the welcome table and head into the galleries, where you are the judge. Which artwork looks the oldest? Which one took the most time to make? Which one tells the best story? Or invent an award of your own. Hold your trophy up (18 inches back from the art), snap a photo of your winner. Receive a free art museum sticker for participating. The challenge runs across three floors. Self-guided, family friendly, and drop-in, so stay for ten minutes or an hour on your way to Memorial Stadium.
Source: Architecture + Design, Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Eskenazi School of Art

item.title: Preventing Campus Violence: Building Community Safety and Accountability — Tue Nov 3, 6:00 PM — Woodburn Hall
item.description:
Middle Way House Club at Indiana University is hosting a discussion about the culture of sexual violence on campus and about skills that build safety and accountability in our community. We want to hold compassion and care together as emotions around rape culture continue to rise. We know as our institutions around us continue to fail and not provide safety, we have to keep our own community safe. During this event we will build the skills of accountability, safety planning, bystander intervention and more. Join us Tuesday the 3rd at 6:00 pm!
Hosted by: Middle Way House Club at IU
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12940901
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: BEYOND BOUNDARIES: Defying Genre Through Collaborative Creative Practice — Thu Nov 5, 4:30 PM — Grunwald Gallery
item.description:
Join IU alumni Anna Butterss (bassist/composer) and Josh Johnson (Grammy-winning saxophonist/producer) for a conversation on navigating cross-genre collaborations, building versatile artistic careers, and transforming foundational IU training into a dynamic, boundary-pushing creative practice. This event is part of the November First Thursdays and is co-hosted by IU Jazz Studies (Jacobs School of Music), IU Arts & Humanities Council, and the Grunwald Gallery (Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design).
Source: Architecture + Design, IU Eskenazi School of Art, IU Jacobs School of Music

item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Nov 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Fri Nov 6 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.description:

item.title: Union Board Out & About Presents: Let's Go Caving! — Fri Nov 6, 12:00 PM — IMU Biddle Hotel Lobby
item.description:
Union Board’s Out & About committee is heading underground, and we’re taking 50 students with us to Marengo Cave, completely free of charge! Meet at the IMU Biddle Hotel Lobby by 12:00 PM, where we'll drive everyone down to Marengo Cave in southern Indiana. Once there, you’ll take the Dripstone Tour, a guided one-mile walk through the cave that takes about an hour. Snacks and bottled water provided. When the tour wraps up, we’ll bring you back to the IMU by around 5:30 PM. No caving experience needed. Just bring a jacket, since it stays cool underground all year. item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Nov 6, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Nov 6, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Animal Hour / Dive Deeper — Fri Nov 6, 3:00 PM — Wonderlab
item.description:
November Theme: Technology Day: Friday Times 3 - 4pm Recommended for: All ages Event Price Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Get closer to the wild side with Animal Hour and Dive Deeper! Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery.
